- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast dip by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > 0.0) and price is trending down, model underestimates fall → add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility in early forecast window (days 1–7) → reduce forecast variance by 15–20% for first 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.0), model fails to capture mean reversion → adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average.
- If model forecast is >+10% above recent 18-day high, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (avg > 0.3).
